hypothesis: Bounded full-trip scalar fission can split independent unconditional add/fadd reductions even when the original scalar producer carries local state. First-order delays, two mutually dependent delays and other scalar producer recurrences need not satisfy LV recurrence recognition or become consumers. Recognizing closed extractable accumulators separately from retained header PHIs removes an unnecessary all-PHIs-are-reductions legality restriction without a pressure/depth/reduction-count profitability model, original-loop vectorizability gate, source rewrite or benchmark-specific rule.
semantics: RecognizeReduction first checks the existing scalar add/fadd shape, supported update placement and compact shape. For an unconditional candidate the accumulator PHI has exactly one use, its update. The update's only users are its own backedge PHI and final Exit LCSSA PHIs. The compact case retains exactly its old update/bypass uses, one-use arm update and final merge exports. Any first edge from accumulator state into a retained recurrence, predicate, address, contribution, another reduction or a partial export therefore prevents extraction, without transitive DAG walks. Nonextractable scalar header PHIs stay in the original producer with their starts, backedges, operations, flags, CFG and execution order. At least one independently extractable reduction remains mandatory. The unchanged loop-wide live-out check rejects every exported retained value, including feedback accumulators, so an independent consumer cannot hide an unsupported export. Any extracted compact reduction combined with retained state rejects; existing compact semantics are not extended. The original CFG/effect/call/load whitelist, strictfp and constrained-FP rejections, trip/termination proofs, scratch limits, ordinal and participating counts, alias behavior and stage metadata remain unchanged. No d2 exports/chunks, calls or memory effects are imported. Ordinary unconstrained unflagged FP retains the per-reduction order and operand order under both settings of the separate fission FP-reordering option; strictfp/constrained execution remains a rejection contract. Eleven new positive fixtures exercise first-order integer/double delay and two-delay state, canonical and bounded affine controls, producer predicates/diamonds, enclosing carry/reuse and capacity edges. A focused checker compares every retained instruction and PHI to the original in block/order (normal LV may only remove integer nowrap flags), certifies completed/ordinal/full-count and scratch provenance, requires actual vector consumers/ordered FP or scalar boundaries, and adds host-only iteration/latch/vector/tail probes. The C harness compares separately compiled original IR, actual transformed paths and independent scalar formulas, including aliases and output canaries. All checks are requested, not claimed run.
costs: No target scratch, schedule or guard algorithm changes. Newly admitted full-trip loops reserve M times each unique contribution's allocation size plus ABI padding, still capped at 65536 bytes and the signed pointer-index ceiling. The new three-reduction fixtures share one i32 stream plus one double stream: accounted reserved scratch is 16/784/3064/65536 bytes at M=1/65/255/5461, with 12 bytes stored and 12 bytes loaded per completed iteration (24*N total), irrespective of two integer accumulators sharing the stream. Enclosing loops reuse the same entry allocation for each row; traffic is 24*sum(row N), capacity does not grow with row count. No recurrence-state arrays, masks or unbounded storage are introduced. Original inputs and helper calls remain once per original iteration/path; no extra original-input rereads, producer duplication or contribution recomputation. Existing original entry guards, ordinary LV vector/tail checks and noncanonical ordinal/completed arithmetic remain; there are no new alias/SCEV/FP guards. Production adds a small optional recognizer, direct PHI/update/merge user scans and a retained-state bit, plus the existing scalar-type check and whole-loop whitelist/live-out scan. Analysis is linear in visited instructions/uses and CFG edges apart from unchanged SCEV queries; no recursive dependence machinery or new profitability model. Harness additions are one focused fixture certificate/matrix and one independent reference family with fixed-size test buffers. Physical stack traffic, spills, target execution, pressure and speedup remain unmeasured.
limitations: This worker ran no compiler, build, test runner or executable comparison. The new transformation, new lit files and new checker shapes all await independent harness validation. Retained state plus compact consumers, producer live-outs, chunk scheduling, arbitrary cyclic producer CFGs, early exits, unsafe calls/stores/volatile/atomics, unavailable/oversized finite bounds and strictfp/constrained FP remain unsupported under their existing contracts. Conditional retained-state merges and pointer recurrences are not separately exercised by the new execution matrix, although producer-local scalar state is admitted by the same unchanged-effect/use proof. The new fixture checker is intentionally bounded to its demonstrated typed IR shapes and three control families; it is not a general IR equivalence solver. Whole-function aggregate scratch budgets are unchanged. Fixed-vscale host execution is not RVV target execution; RVV machine verification is not a speedup measurement. No corpus selection increase, speedup, maturity or t000036 merge outcome is claimed.
test_expectations: All eleven new positive functions formerly fail the old requirement that every non-control header PHI be a supported reduction; each now has actual original/transformed/independent execution coverage requested, including ordered FP and integer results. No pre-existing correctness obligation is removed.

Two existing affine feedback rejection remarks change from scalar-unsupported-recurrence to scalar-unsupported-live-out: feedback prevents extraction of that accumulator, which is retained, and its exported final value then fails the unchanged producer live-out check. Their no-split and result checks remain. Existing single-accumulator rejection diagnostics retain their first recognition failure when nothing can be extracted.

New rejections cover accumulator PHI/update/predicate/address/other-reduction feedback, partial accumulator exports, retained state exports, stores/effectful calls, unavailable bounds, the first over-capacity mixed stream (5462), strictfp/constrained FP, no extractable add/fadd, and retained state with compact participation.

The new checker test uses actual scalar and LV2 vector/tail output. Positives include SSA-renamed retained recurrences and normal LV removal of integer nowrap flags. Mutations preserve all inherited checker tests and reject wrong recurrence starts/backedges/operands/opcodes/order, moved/duplicated state work, wrong scratch capacity/index/store count, bound-as-consumer-count and FP reassociation.
